status: Unpublished constrained-fit candidate; inspect candidate-validation report before integration

sources.review: Figure 2 on PDF page 7 visually inspected again. Distributor shaft, separate intermediate drive and pump share a straight drive path beside the camshaft. Industrial comparison only; perspective and drawing scale do not establish truck angle, mounting station or dimensions.
IS-74: 4.520 inch length, .312 inch hex, L & M ends, hardened steel. Exact end details and fit tolerances absent.
Previously reviewed manufacturer 1994 F-150 4.9L application lists IS-74.
Truck catalog identifies intermediate shaft C5AZ6A618A; no dimensions supplied.

sourced_constraints.drive_sequence: camshaft to distributor to intermediate shaft to rotor pump

provisional_solution.pump_mount: Two illustrative block-connected columns and angled mounting feet reuse the outboard provisional housing ears; separate smooth-shank bolts. This is not reconstructed production mounting architecture.

reasoning: X station lies between existing cam lobes and avoids moving the sourced bore/stroke architecture.
Nearest points on perpendicular cam and tilted distributor axes define the gear centers, rather than arbitrarily bridging the old display datums.
The provisional distributor upper neck length increases so the full-size bowl clears the existing pushrod cover without cutting a hole through the cover.
The lower distributor shaft extends into a matching hex socket while the manufacturer-length intermediate shaft remains unchanged.
Pump upper drive shaft grows locally to retain wall thickness around the larger sourced hex; the housing bore grows with it.
Pickup bell and screen retain their existing sump locations. A hollow swept tube connects the moved inlet to that bell.
limits: Collision-free fit and sampled gear motion do not establish OEM dimensions, backlash, tooth contact stress, lubrication, friction or operating durability.
Retainer remains a separate illustrative split-ring envelope. Exact gripping construction and production seating remain unresolved.
Pump gerotor curves remain inherited non-conjugate illustrations. Full pumping motion and oil-pressure simulation are not claimed.
Block mounting supports and socket changes are CAD interface studies, never machining or repair instructions.
